introduction.text: The Cappella di Reginald Pole is a small historic chapel in Rome, built by Cardinal Reginald Pole in 1539 as a memorial to a thwarted assassination attempt. It exemplifies Roman classical architectural style and houses a Marian icon.

history.description: Construction of the chapel by Cardinal Reginald Pole in 1539, following a failed assassination attempt by King Henry VIII.
The chapel was transferred to the Venerabile Collegio Inglese and later abandoned and desacralized in the early 20th century, with its portals sealed.

design.description: The chapel is a small, elegant structure echoing Roman classical tombs, featuring eight yellow brick lesenes with granite plinths and capitals, a travertine entablature, a cupola, four small windows, and two perpendicular portals.

art.description: An original Marian icon once housed inside the chapel.
